description: A Trie is a tree in which each root-to-node path spells a prefix of some inserted string, giving O(L) insert, search, and prefix-check regardless of how many strings are stored. It converts repeated dictionary lookups, prefix queries, and grid word searches from per-word scans into a single shared traversal, and its bitwise variant unlocks O(32) max-XOR queries.
important_details: Each node holds children (a 26-slot array for lowercase, or a HashMap for larger/unknown alphabets) plus an isEndOfWord flag.
Prefix queries are the trie's unique strength: no hash-based structure answers 'does any stored word start with X' as cheaply.
search() must check isEndOfWord at the terminal node; startsWith() must NOT — conflating them is the standard bug.
Storing the full word (or a payload) at terminal nodes often removes the need to rebuild strings during traversal.
A bitwise trie over the 32-bit representation of integers turns O(n^2) pairwise-XOR problems into O(n * 32).
other_relevant_details: Trigger words: 'prefix', 'starts with', 'autocomplete', 'dictionary', 'word list', or repeated queries against a fixed set of strings. Space is the main cost — a 26-slot array per node is fast but memory-hungry; switch to a HashMap when the alphabet is large or the trie is sparse. When memory is tight and the word set is static, a sorted array plus binary search on prefixes is a valid lighter alternative.

variations.description: The foundational trie supporting exact-word insertion, exact-word lookup, and prefix existence checks, all in O(L).
important_details: insert() walks and creates nodes per character, marking isEnd only at the final character.
A failed traversal (missing child) short-circuits both search and startsWith immediately.
Use a 26-slot array for guaranteed-lowercase input; use HashMap<Character, Node> when the alphabet is unknown or large.
Deletion is the rarely-practiced operation: unmark isEnd, then prune nodes bottom-up only while they have no children and are not terminal for another word.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(L) per operation. Space: O(total characters inserted * alphabet size) worst case.

variations.description: Extend search to support a wildcard character that matches any single letter, requiring DFS branching into every child whenever a wildcard is encountered.
important_details: On a normal character, descend into exactly one child; on a wildcard, recurse into ALL non-null children.
Worst-case time degrades to O(26^L) when the pattern is all wildcards, but real inputs prune heavily.
The recursion must pass the current index through, since the wildcard branch explores multiple subtrees at the same depth.
Return true as soon as any branch succeeds — do not keep exploring after a match is found.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(L) with no wildcards, up to O(26^L) in the pathological all-wildcard case. Space: O(L) recursion depth.

problems.name: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

variations.variation: Trie + Backtracking on a Grid (Word Search II)
variations.description: Search a 2D letter grid for an entire dictionary at once by building one trie of all target words and running a single DFS that prunes any path which stops matching a trie prefix.
important_details: One shared trie means one DFS pass finds all words, instead of O(words) separate searches.
Store the complete word at its terminal node so you can add it to the result without rebuilding the string.
Set the terminal node's word to null after collecting it, which both de-duplicates results and prunes future search.
Mark visited cells by temporarily mutating the grid (e.g. to '#') and restore on backtrack — an explicit visited matrix also works but costs more space.
Advanced pruning: physically remove leaf nodes from the trie once their word is found, shrinking the search space as you go.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(rows * cols * 4^L) worst case, but trie pruning makes real runtimes far lower. Space: O(sum of word lengths).

variations.description: Use a trie to accelerate dictionary membership tests inside DP or DFS word-breaking problems, walking the trie character by character instead of slicing substrings and hashing them.
important_details: In Word Break, for each start index walk the trie forward; every terminal node encountered marks a valid split point for the DP.
This avoids building O(n^2) substring objects, which matters for long strings even though both approaches are asymptotically similar.
Word Break II must memoize by start index, caching the list of sentences from that index, or it blows up exponentially on adversarial input.
Concatenated Words is the same machinery with the rule that a word must decompose into at least two OTHER dictionary words — sort by length and build the trie incrementally.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(n^2) worst case but with much smaller constants and early termination than substring hashing. Space: O(dictionary size + n).

variations.description: Support prefix-based suggestion queries by descending to the prefix node and either DFS-collecting all words below it, or reading a precomputed top-k list cached at every node.
important_details: DFS-on-demand: O(prefix length + size of subtree), simple but slow when the subtree is huge.
Precomputed top-k: store a small sorted list at each node during insertion, giving O(prefix length + k) queries at the cost of extra space.
For ranked suggestions, store a frequency/hotness score at terminal nodes and use a bounded min-heap while collecting.
Lexicographic ordering comes free if you iterate children in alphabetical order during the DFS.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(prefix length + k) per query with precomputation. Space: O(total characters * k).

variations.description: Build a binary trie over the bit representations of integers (MSB to LSB) so that the maximum XOR against any stored number is found greedily in O(32) instead of O(n) per query.
important_details: At each bit, greedily descend into the OPPOSITE bit of the query number to set that bit of the XOR result to 1.
If the opposite branch is absent, you are forced down the same-bit branch and that XOR bit is 0.
Depth is fixed at 32 (or fewer if constraints bound the values), independent of how many numbers are inserted — this is why it beats O(n^2) brute force.
For offline queries with an upper-bound constraint (XOR with elements <= m), sort both the array and the queries and insert incrementally.
Storing a subtree minimum at each node lets you answer bounded-value queries without rebuilding the trie.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(n * 32) to build, O(32) per query. Space: O(n * 32) nodes worst case.

variations.description: Insert every suffix of a string (or reversed words) into a trie so that substring queries, suffix matching, and combined prefix-suffix lookups become prefix queries on the trie.
important_details: Inserting all n suffixes costs O(n^2) time and space — acceptable only for short strings; a suffix automaton or suffix array is the scalable alternative.
For 'search by suffix', insert reversed words so a suffix becomes a prefix.
Prefix-and-Suffix Search is elegantly solved by inserting every 'suffix#word' concatenation, turning a two-sided query into a single prefix lookup.
Stream of Characters inserts reversed dictionary words and queries the reversed recent-character stream.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(maximum word length) per query. Space: O(sum of word lengths * alphabet size).

variations.description: Augment each node with a prefix count and a word count so you can report how many stored words share a prefix, and delete words correctly by decrementing counts rather than blindly pruning.
important_details: prefixCount at a node = how many inserted words pass through it; wordCount = how many words terminate exactly there.
countWordsStartingWith is then an O(L) lookup returning prefixCount, with no subtree traversal at all.
Deletion decrements prefixCount along the path and wordCount at the terminal; only physically remove a node when its prefixCount reaches zero.
Never delete a node just because isEnd became false — other longer words may still pass through it. This is the single most common trie-deletion bug.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(L) for insert, count, and erase. Space: O(total characters * alphabet size).
